say: Prioritize unprompted return, not audio superiority—but call it a repeat-use signal, not a proven habit. Your unresolved question is: will commuters seek a second episode without a founder reminder? Proposed test: invite ten SSE commuters, offer one initial episode, and explain once where and when the next two will appear. uncertainty: Instructors running recurring cardboard craft sessions lose preparation time adapting existing projects to available materials and session length.
Provider managers with discretionary activity budgets could authorize €10 monthly if matching saves enough instructor time; neither the price nor willingness to pay is established.

Proposed test: within €20, invite five Riga instructors through public professional contacts, ask about their most recent planning episode and identify the actual budget owner. Offer a voluntary, instructor-supervised pilot for one defined age band using only human-reviewed cards.

Predeclare a usefulness threshold: two instructors each run two matched projects and report at least 10 minutes less preparation per session versus their usual method. Separately test payment by asking an authorized buyer to purchase continuation at the stated €10 monthly price; buying another week
How often material-and-duration mismatch occurs, which age band experiences it, and whether cardboard projects are frequent enough to support repeat use.
dissent: The Riga teaching-materials event could indicate an existing source of useful resources rather than an unmet paid need.
A small curated library may solve the problem without generation or automatic emailing.
Five invitations can test recruitment feasibility but cannot reliably distinguish weak demand from poor outreach.

say: Start instructor-first, but require an introduction to the person who can authorize payment before offering the pilot. Treat this as a hypothesis, not an established best channel. R5237cb0f8597 concerns educators’ practice-sharing; it does not establish purchasing authority or demand for paid project cards. Your unresolved question is whether instructor interest can turn into provider spending—not merely whether instructors will try a craft. Run one small, two-route test within the proposed €20 outreach budget: approach five distinct providers through instructors and five comparable providers through managers. Use the same offer and deadline.
